column2: the broken window on the back wall, with its torn curtain and bent rod.
column3: In its exact place and at its exact size and shape, a brand new arched window: a fresh clean white painted wooden frame with the same arch and the same four panes, all of them whole, clear bright glass showing pale blue sky with one soft white cloud, a chunky new brass curtain rod, and two new sunflower yellow curtains tied back neatly on both sides with plain round ties. No planks, no cracks and no holes remain.

column2: the broken ceiling lamp hanging from the ceiling, with its cobwebs.
column3: In its exact place and at its exact size, a brand new chandelier: a chunky polished warm brass frame on a short straight chain with three round warm cream glass shades, all three lit and glowing a soft warm yellow, hanging perfectly straight. The cobwebs around it are gone.

column2: the broken stone fireplace on the right, with its chimney breast, the cracked mantel, the crooked empty picture frame above it and the rubble on its hearth.
column3: In its exact place and at its exact size and shape, a brand new fireplace: smooth warm cream stone with a chunky clean mantelpiece, no cracks, the hearth swept clean, and a cheerful fire burning inside on two logs: big simple rounded flame shapes in sunflower yellow and warm orange, glowing softly on the hearth. Above the mantel the picture frame now hangs straight and holds a simple painting of a sunny green hill under blue sky. A small green potted plant stands on one end of the mantel.

column2: the old torn sofa standing against the left wall, with its dust sheet.
column3: In its exact place, facing the same way, at the same size and in the same perspective, a brand new three-seat sofa: chunky and rounded, upholstered in warm coral orange, plump whole seat and back cushions, two round sunflower yellow scatter cushions, standing level on four short wooden legs. No dust sheet, no rips, no stuffing.

column2: the torn faded oval rug lying flat in the middle of the floor.
column3: In its exact place, at the same size and lying flat in the same perspective, a brand new oval rug: whole and soft, a plain warm cream centre with two plain wide flat bands of teal and coral around its edge, no fringe, no holes, no fine pattern. Nothing stands on it.

column2: all the mess on the floor: the cardboard boxes and broken planks in the front left corner, the planks leaning against the wall beside the fireplace, the tipped bucket and the plaster lumps in the front right corner, and every small lump of rubble lying anywhere on the floor.
column3: All of it is gone. In its place is the plain clean wooden floor of the room, the same planks continuing in the same colour, direction and perspective as the rest of the floor, swept clean and whole, with no object of any kind on it.

column2: the walls and the ceiling: the peeling teal wallpaper with its curled torn flaps and cracks, the cracked ceiling, and the cobwebs in the corners of the ceiling.
column3: The walls are freshly papered in a clean bright teal with the same wide plain vertical stripes, smooth and whole with no flaps, no tears and no cracks, a fresh warm white skirting and cornice, and a clean smooth cream ceiling with no cracks and no cobwebs. The window, the lamp, the fireplace and all the furniture stay exactly as they are, still broken.
